title: Super Smash Bros. is ready for its unofficial Android port
summary: You can't play it on Switch, but unsanctioned Android ports could be coming soon.
body: TL;DR Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 64 has been fully decompiled, opening the door to unofficial native ports. The 1999 platform fighter hasn’t been available through official means for several years and isn’t currently playable on Nintendo Switch consoles. We aren’t aware of any ports made from the newly decompiled code yet, but we expect they’ll start appearing soon. Aside from some high-profile rereleases, present-day Nintendo is notoriously stingy when it comes to providing easy, legitimate access to its immense back catalog of classic games. This, in part, has inspired fans to take matters into their own hands by decompiling old favorites, recreating their source code so the games can be easily (if unofficially) ported to modern platforms like Windows or Android. Now, another classic that’s been inaccessible on modern hardware is ripe for porting: 1999’s Super Smash Bros. has been fully decompiled. As shared on Decomp.dev , Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 64 is now “100.00% decompiled,” meaning the game’s source code has been completely recreated and it’s ready to be ported. Compared to emulated games, ports created from decompiled source code can run natively on modern hardw…

title: Dexter and the Moonrocks Want ‘to Set the Tone of What Rock Music Is Going to Be’
summary: How the fast-rising grunge band is shaping what “a new rock star is.”
body: “We’re four dumbasses from West Texas — like us or hate us, this is who we are,” drummer Ryan Fox (commonly referred to as just Fox) says matter-of-­factly of a band that has both helped to resurrect the sound of ’90s grunge and bring them back to the Billboard charts. The four members of Dexter and the Moonrocks started out exploring red-dirt country but have surged to the forefront of the current rock revival with songs that marry country’s confessional lyrics (“I’m a bad guy” stories, as guitarist Ryan Anderson puts it) with grunge’s heavy guitars, acoustic introspection and affinity for strong melody. The resulting sound — they’ve dubbed it “Western space grunge,” the name of their July 2024 debut EP — is powered by singer James Tuffs’ ­magnetic, raw vocals and can evoke everything from Alice in Chains to Weezer. After getting together outside Abilene and releasing its debut single in 2021, the band began a still-relentless live schedule, getting signed by Severance Records in a joint venture with Big Loud Rock in 2023 and making its alternative radio breakthrough the following year. But it wasn’t until earlier this year that Dexter and the Moonrocks became a true commercial f…

title: Duetti Opens Office in Nashville’s Music Row
summary: The company is closing in on having 100 employees since it first began four years ago, Duetti's CEO Lior Tibon says.
body: Catalog investment firm Duetti has opened a new Music City office, located in Nashville’s Music Row area at 1604 16th Ave. S, Billboard can reveal. The move brings the company’s A&R, publishing and marketing teams under one roof to deepen the company’s partnerships with Nashville-based writers and artists, in order to serve Nashville’s music community, spanning genres including country, Americana, pop, R&B, Gospel, hip-hop and more. title: Google is working on a big Live Translate upgrade for Android XR
summary: Listening area in Google Translate may offer extensive control over the Live Translate feature for Android XR-based devices.
body: TL;DR Google Translate could introduce big Live Translate updates for the Android XR platform. We have exclusively uncovered traces of a “Listening area” feature that will offer extensive control over the microphones. If implemented, users will be able to switch between Front-only and Surrounding-area mic modes for Live Translate on Android XR. While there’s only one Android XR device on the market right now, namely the Samsung Galaxy XR, there are more on the way. Google has already built deep integrations for its core apps like Google Maps, Photos, Gboard, and the Play Store. Last year, we uncovered development on Live Translate for Google’s extended reality platform. We can now exclusively reveal a potential feature addition for the Live Translate experience on Android XR. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. Authority Insights brings you all the latest exclusive reports, app teardowns, leaks, and in-depth tech coverage from the Android Authority team that you won’t find anywhere else.

title: The next wide-screen foldable may have just leaked in real-world images
summary: New leaked images offer a closer look at Xiaomi’s mysterious wide-screen foldable.
body: TL;DR Xiaomi’s next foldable has leaked, showing a wide inner display and a design that closely resembles the company’s own HyperOS 4 teaser. The XRing O3 will power the device, with a 10-core CPU, Arm’s new G2-Ultra NX GPU, and eye-catching performance claims. The Xiaomi 18 Fold launches in September, but key details such as global availability, pricing, and dimensions remain unknown. Xiaomi’s XRing O3 chipset has already made headlines with some seriously ambitious performance claims, but the chip’s first phone may be just as interesting. Xiaomi has confirmed that the 3nm processor will debut in the Xiaomi 18 Fold next month, and now leaked images appear to show the company’s upcoming foldable in the flesh. The images, which Digital Chat Station (DCS) shared on Weibo , show a book-style foldable with a wide inner display similar to the Galaxy Z Fold 8 , relatively thick bezels, and a punch-hole selfie camera near the upper-right corner. One image also shows the rear of the device, including a large camera module, but it doesn’t reveal enough to say much about its hardware.

title: Nothing unveils Nothing OS 5.0 built on Android 17, but there’s bad news for older phones
summary: Older phones will not be receiving this update, as expected.
body: TL;DR Nothing has announced Nothing OS 5.0, bringing a massive overhaul featuring the Geist typeface, translucent software layering, dynamic wallpaper-tinted adaptive themes, and dedicated apps for both the Glyph Interface and Essential Apps Builder. The update also introduces Android 17 platform features such as split notification and Quick Settings panels, cross-platform Quick Share with iOS, enhanced privacy indicators, and more. Open Beta testing for the Nothing Phone 3 starts tomorrow, with a full stable release expected in mid-October. However, Phone 1, Phone 2, and CMF Phone 1 will not receive the update. Nothing has officially revealed Nothing OS 5.0, detailing the next major evolution of its custom Android skin. Built on top of Android 17 , the platform update brings a visual design overhaul, expanded lock screen personalization, new first-party widgets, and tighter system-level integration with the Glyph Interface. Following an announcement teased on X , Nothing published a detailed breakdown of the new features and the design evolution on its community forums.

title: How Sam Fender & Olivia Dean’s ‘Rein Me In’ Became the U.K.’s Longest-Running No. 1 Single Ever
summary: The song now holds the all-time record for the longest-running U.K. No. 1 single.
body: Sam Fender ’s show at the London Stadium in June 2025 remains momentous for many reasons. It was the midway point of the rollout of his Mercury Prize-winning LP People Watching , and also his largest ever headline show. But perhaps the most consequential moment from it came midway through the set, album deep cut “Rein Me In” got an airing, with the show’s support act Olivia Dean , then a rising star, joining on vocals for a new verse. Now their careers — and that song — appear unstoppable. “Rein Me In” is in record-breaking territory on the U.K.’s Official Singles Chart. The track has earned 22 weeks at No. 1, and became the longest-running No. 1 single of the 21st century after 16, surpassing Drake’s “Hotline Bling.” It has now pulled clear of Frankie Laine’s “I Believe” in the all time rankings, which notched 18 weeks at the summit back in 1953, to become the longest-running U.K. No. 1 single ever. In February, it earned the BRIT Awards’ publicly voted song of the year prize, with Dean and Fender on hand to collect the prize in Manchester. Amid chart dominance in early May, Dean returned the favor by inviting Fender to give the son…

title: Writer Liz Meriwether Has Been Listening to Britney Spears ‘A Lot’ While Writing Script For ‘The Woman in Me’ Biopic
summary: Since you asked, her favorite songs at the moment are deep cuts "Perfume" (from 2013's Britney Jean) and "If I'm Dancing" (from 2016's Glory).
body: New Girl and Furious screenwriter Liz Meriwether has been doing all the things one does when preparing for a biopic on one of the world’s most famous pop icons. She’s listening to the Michelle Williams-read audiobook of Britney Spears ‘ 2023 The Woman in Me memoir, and, in news that should warm the hearts of the Britney Army, she is seemingly doing a deep dive into Brit’s music, at least as evidenced by which tracks she told The Hollywood Reporter are her current favorites from the singer’s nine-LP catalog. Meriwether spoke to the magazine about the task of adapting the tell-all into a film and though details of what the movie will look, and sound like are scarce, she did delve into her prep for the project that will team her with the creative hive mind behind the pair of hit Wicked films, director Jon M. Chu and producer Marc Platt; Universal has not yet confirmed any details about the adaptation. Meriwether told THR that it’s still early in the process, but she’s spoken to Chu and Platt “so much” already and found them to be very collaborative. “I’m so used to being the final word on everything,” she said of…

title: New leak suggests Qualcomm’s next Snapdragon 8 Elite could take it to the extreme, literally
summary: Qualcomm's naming convention is getting further out of hand.
body: TL;DR According to a new leak, Qualcomm’s next flagship chip will be called the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. It could feature two prime cores clocked at 5.01GHz, along with three performance and three efficiency cores. The Dimensity 9600 Pro could also use two prime cores clocked at 4.55GHz, along with three performance and three efficiency cores. Qualcomm and MediaTek are both gearing up to launch their latest flagship processors. The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 series and the MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro are expected to feature improvements across the board. Now, a new leak is shedding some light on the core arrangement and clock speeds of the top-of-the-line Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and the Dimensity 9600 Pro. According to a Weibo post by Digital Chat Station (DCS), the upcoming Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro, model number SM8975, could be called the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 instead. The extremely long (pun intended) and unnecessarily weird name notwithstanding, Qualcomm’s next flagship chip seems set to break the 5GHz barrier for smartphone chipsets.

title: Galaxy S26 series gets sixth One UI 9 beta release, but when is the stable update coming?
summary: The latest 851MB update targets several UI and routine issues for global users ahead of the stable launch.
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung has released the sixth One UI 9 beta for the Galaxy S26 series. The 851MB update (firmware ZZHE) includes the August 5, 2026, security patch and fixes key issues, including display errors with the Now Brief widget and photo-saving issues in Expert RAW 24MP at specific focal lengths. Currently live in Germany, India, Poland, the UK, and South Korea, the new update will soon be available in the US as well. Samsung entered One UI 9 development with much gusto, but after releasing the stable update alongside the new Galaxy Z8 foldables, the pace of One UI 9 beta releases for its previous flagships has slowed down a bit. After releasing the fifth One UI 9 beta almost two weeks ago, Samsung is now picking things up with the sixth One UI 9 beta release for the Galaxy S26 series. We’ve received the sixth One UI 9 update on our Galaxy S26 Ultra in the UK. This Android 17-based update comes with firmware version ending in ZZHE, the August 5, 2026 security patch, and is 851MB in size.

title: 5 reasons I may not go back to Spotify after trying YouTube Music
summary: YouTube Music isn't perfect, but you can't ignore the value proposition.
body: As is the case with millions of users around the world, I’ve been a loyal Spotify subscriber for as long as I can remember. The app works well across Android and iOS, there’s a great selection of music, and features like Jam and Spotify Connect have made my listening experience much more seamless across audio devices at home. I was happy to pay for the Premium Duo plan — until it was sneakily taken away. Spotify removed the Duo plan in India around November 2025, but as I had subscribed to it long before, I was able to continue with it, as it should be. Then came the email, one July morning this year, saying my Premium Duo plan was canceled due to an “issue” with my payment method. Nothing had changed, so it didn’t make any sense. I figured it was Spotify forcing me to upgrade to a higher-priced plan, and as it turned out, I wasn’t the only one who got the boot. Frustrated with this move, I decided to try other options.

title: Busta Rhymes Releases J Dilla-Produced ‘Dillagence II’ Project Featuring D’Angelo, Lil Wayne, Ludacris & Big Sean: Stream It Now
summary: A sequel to Busta and Dilla's 2007 mixtape is here.
body: Nearly 20 years after the original, Busta Rhymes has posthumously collaborated with the late J Dilla to release their joint Dillagence II project. The anticipated sequel arrived on streaming services on Tuesday (Aug. 25). The project boasts 19 tracks and is loaded with a range of features, including Dilla’s mother, Ma Dukes, R&B legend D’Angelo, Big Sean, Ludacris, Lil Wayne, Common, Talib Kweli, Anderson .Paak and upstarts like La Reezy and Honey Bxby. D’Angelo, who passed away from pancreatic cancer in 2025, appears on “This Woman” and Busta revealed that the track came from an unfinished collab between the Voodoo singer and J Dilla over 20 years ago. “I was gifted with something that they did that they didn’t finish when the word started to spread about this project. I didn’t know that it existed because it was done 20-something years ago,” Busta told New York Times’ Popcast . “They started something and it just never got finished. I love both of them, so I wanted to do whatever justice I could do and continue to uphold the legacies of these brothers.” Busta also teased a music video for “This Wom…

title: After just 5 days, my Pixel 11 Pro is already a brick
summary: This isn't a great start.
body: The Pixel lineup and hardware woes seem to go hand in hand. Whether it’s OLED tint issues with the Pixel 2 XL, overheating, spontaneously shattering camera glass, or display issues with the Pixel 9 Pro lineup, hardware troubles seem constant. As a day-one Pixel user ever since the first phone launched, I’ve usually been immune to all the troubles that tend to plague Google’s flagship. Well, as the saying goes, luck eventually does run out. I’ve had my Pixel 11 Pro for just five days, and it’s already a brick. A couple of days into my time with the Pixel 11 Pro (in the gorgeous Canyon colorway), I decided to do a factory reset and a fresh setup instead of copying over all my data from my previous phone, and here we are.

title: The Galaxy Z Fold 8 has a camera problem, and it has nothing to do with photo quality
summary: Samsung put the Galaxy Z Fold 8's folding display selfie camera in the worst spot.
body: I’ve spent years trying the latest book-style foldables, but none earned a permanent spot in my pocket once I finished testing them. Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 7 came the closest with a thin-and-light design and truly flagship specs. Unfortunately, it suffered from the same problems as every other folding phone with a squarish inner screen aspect ratio. The form factor isn’t conducive to widescreen video content, as you’ll see large black bars at the top and bottom of the folding screen. Samsung built the wide Galaxy Z Fold 8 to specifically address this pain point, and it quickly won me over. Then, something happened that I didn’t expect. I found myself using the Galaxy Z Fold 8 unfolded in portrait orientation more than landscape.

title: Sony’s new phone is one of your only options with microSD support, but it’s not all roses
summary: Hey Sony, how about upgrading something?
body: TL;DR The Xperia 10 VIII is official with the exact same hardware as the Xperia 10 VII. It comes with the Snapdragon 6 Gen 3, 8GB of RAM, and 128GB of storage. The cameras are also exactly the same as the Xperia 10 VII, and the display is 50% brighter. After a couple of leaks , Sony has finally announced the new Xperia 10 VIII, and it’s basically the same phone as the Xperia 10 VII, bar one small upgrade and a new paint job. The Xperia 10 VIII looks almost exactly the same as the Xperia 10 VII. There’s the horizontal camera bar on the back, “Sony” branding on the camera island, and a front that looks remarkably out of date with thicker bezels on the top and bottom. It also retains the fingerprint scanner and the 3.5mm headphone jack, and Sony claims that the stereo speakers are now 30% louder.

title: We tried Gemini’s new Device Help feature on the Pixel 11, and the results were mixed
summary: Gemini is ready to fix your Pixel, well, almost ready.
body: TL;DR Gemini’s experimental Device Help feature is appearing in the Gemini app on Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro devices, letting you troubleshoot your phone using natural language. It can diagnose battery and Wi-Fi issues, open specific settings, change things like brightness and dark mode, and explain Pixel features without making you hunt through Settings. It’s still a Labs feature and can get things wrong. Our testing produced inconsistent instructions for Magic Capture, so it isn’t completely reliable yet. A few days ago, we spotted Google testing a clever new Gemini trick that could save Pixel users from digging through the Settings app every time something goes wrong. That feature, called Device Help, is now appearing directly inside the Gemini app on some of our Pixel 11 series devices. First spotted by 9to5Google , Device Help is currently showing up on Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro models we’ve checked, including our Pixel 11 Pro XL units. It still has a “Labs” badge attached, though, which is Google’s way of telling you things may not always work as expected. And after putting it through a few tests, that’s exactly what we found.

title: Google’s Tensor G7 has one last chance to save the Pixel 12
summary: Dubious silicon is detracting from Pixel's best features.
body: The Pixel 11 series has left Google with something of a dilemma. Based on our time with the phones so far, they remain among the most enjoyable Android handsets to use, thanks largely to Google’s software experience and a growing collection of genuinely useful features. But our testing of the Tensor G6 shows that Google’s custom silicon is falling further behind rival flagship chips; early gaming tests suggest a familiar litany of issues; and a week with the Pixel 11 Pro suggests that many of Google’s newest AI tricks aren’t yet strong enough to make up the difference. That’s not necessarily a problem for the Pixel 11, but it could become one for the Pixel 12.

title: Vince Staples Announces 2027 Australian Headline Tour
summary: The shows mark his first solo Australian dates in nearly a decade.
body: Vince Staples is heading back to Australia. The “Norf Norf” rapper has announced a run of headline shows for January 2027 in support of his latest album Cry Baby , marking his first solo Australian dates in nearly a decade. Presented by Untitled Group and Beyond the Valley , the Cry Baby Tour will take in Perth, Brisbane, Sydney and Melbourne, wrapping around Staples’ set at Beyond the Valley, the sold-out Victorian festival where he is among the headliners. The run marks his first headline shows in the country since 2018. The tour supports Cry Baby , Staples’ seventh studio album, released in June via Section Eight Arthouse, Loma Vista and Concord. A departure from the introspective, hometown-focused work of 2022’s Ramona Park Broke My Heart and 2024’s Dark Times , the album is a more outward-facing piece of social commentary built around live instrumentation, and was trailed by videos for “Blackberry Marmalade,” “White Flag” and “Cotton.” Staples has been performing the material with a live band, a shift he first showcased at his sold-out Los Angeles album-release show. The Long Beach, California, native bro…

title: Spotify has good news if your audiobooks suddenly stopped playing
summary: But some are still unable to play chapters despite the reported fix.
body: TL;DR Spotify experienced an outage that prevented listeners from playing or downloading audiobooks across multiple devices. The issue has officially been marked as resolved, though a few users report that playback glitches remain. Users still affected should update the app and report the issue on the Help board. Spotify has been steadily adding more reasons to spend time with audiobooks, from narrated magazine articles to TV-style recaps and Playlist Notes . But today, some listeners were unable to play those audiobooks at all, and Spotify now says the problem has been fixed. The issue surfaced earlier today, with Reddit reports coming from users across phones, desktops, and the web. Spotify acknowledged the problem through its Community forum, saying it had received reports that audiobook playback was not working properly and that the relevant teams were working on a fix.

title: The AYN Odin 3 is getting another price hike, but you can avoid it by acting fast
summary: You'll need to act fast to avoid the price increase.
body: Credit: AYN TL;DR AYN has announced another price increase for the Odin 3 handheld. The increase ranges from $20 to $30, meaning the Odin 3 now starts at $369. This is still the only Android handheld with what is effectively the Snapdragon 8 Elite chipset, though. The AYN Odin 3 is the most powerful Android handheld on the market right now, making it ideal for cutting-edge emulation and other demanding games. It’s already seen price hikes this year due to the RAM crisis, but we’ve now got more bad news. AYN announced on Discord that it’ll be raising the price of the Odin 3 once again. These price hikes vary from $20 to $30. Check out the new prices below.

title: Google’s clever Android 17 motion sickness feature is finally rolling out
summary: Pixel phones appear to be the first devices to get Google's Motion Assist feature.
body: TL;DR Google is gradually rolling out the new Motion Assist feature on Android 17 devices, starting with Pixel phones. The feature is designed to reduce motion sickness by displaying motion cues on the screen while you’re in a moving vehicle. Motion Assist is available through Google Play Settings and can automatically activate in a moving vehicle or be controlled manually through a Quick Settings tile. Google is gradually rolling out its new Motion Assist feature on Android 17 , starting with Pixel phones. The feature helps users reduce motion sickness when using their phones in a moving vehicle. title: Spotify bug leaves Android Auto drivers staring at error message
summary: Spotify not working for you on Android Auto? You're not alone.
body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Android Auto users are reporting issues with Spotify. The app is displaying an error message that reads “Spotify isn’t responding.” It’s unclear what the cause of the problem is. Sometimes being an Android Auto user can feel like playing a game of whack-a-mole. A bug appears, a fix is rolled out, and another bug appears shortly after. For example, a fix for a glitch that caused connections to drop or freeze was recently released . Now, a new bug has shown up, and it’s preventing users from streaming their music and podcasts. According to several Android Auto users on Reddit ( 1 , 2 ), the latest issue affects the Spotify app. When attempting to access the app, these users are running into an error message that reads “Spotify isn’t responding.” The screen includes options to exit the app or to wait for it to start working again.

title: The Pixel 11 Pro XL is built to last and easy to fix, teardown finds
summary: It's pricey, but at least you'll be able to hold onto it a few years.
body: TL;DR JerryRigEverything’s Zack Nelson has tested the Pixel 11 Pro XL’s durability and repairability. The phone didn’t bend in Nelson’s durability test, and key components are relatively simple to swap out. Nelson calls the Pixel 11 Pro XL “one of the easiest phones to repair of 2026.” It looks like it should be relatively easy to make the Pixel 11 Pro last. The XL version has now undergone the JerryRigEverything treatment, and the phone held up nicely to Zack Nelson’s usual battery of abuse. The teardown video also shows that common repairs should be relatively simple, with both the display and the battery removable with just a few minutes of work. The video shows that the 11 Pro XL barely bends or flexes at all as Nelson wrenches on it, so the phone should hold up fine in case you sit down with it in your back pocket. Despite Google’s claim that the 11 Pro’s display is “more than twice as scratch-resistant than previous models” thanks to a new coating, though, it still scratches at level six with deeper grooves at a level seven.

title: Netflix is reportedly in talks to add rival streamers like Peacock
summary: Netflix could soon open up its service to other streamers.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Netflix could soon let you access other rival streamers through its platform. The company is reportedly in talks with Peacock and Fox One. It’s unclear if Netflix would sell subscriptions to those streamers or just include their content directly in the app. From Peacock to ESPN , there’s been a rash of streaming-related price hikes lately. If you’re worried that this article will be about Netflix announcing a rate increase, you can rest easy. That’s not happening, at least not yet anyway. Rather, this has to do with Netflix reportedly opening up its service to its rivals. It appears that Netflix is interested in becoming a one-stop shop for streaming. The New York Times reports that Netflix is considering adding shows and movies from other streaming services. The company is said to be currently in talks with Peacock and Fox One to bring their content to the platform.

title: The Galaxy S27 Ultra may debut with self-healing glass
summary: Android Authority remembers the LG G Flex 2.
body: TL;DR A rumor claims glass used in the Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra could come with a self-healing layer that fills in minor scratches on its own. The glass is purportedly being developed jointly by Corning and Samsung. The Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra may introduce an interesting feature that sounds like it could be a real benefit to users. A rumor from this weekend claims that Samsung’s upcoming Ultra flagship will come with self-healing glass that’s able to recover from minor scratches on its own. Late last week, industry observer Schrödinger took to X to say that Corning and Samsung are jointly working on “ a new self-healing surface coating” for the next iteration of the former’s Gorilla Armor glass. This coating would certainly be less scratch-resistant than conventional tempered glass, but if it’s able to fill in hairline scratches on its own, that trade-off could be worth it.

title: Apple’s 20th anniversary iPhone could take some inspiration from Android phones
summary: A leaked render of the 20th anniversary iPhone reveals a radical new redesign, with some familiar elements.
body: TL;DR Apple may be prepping radical design changes for the 20th anniversary iPhone, according to a new leak. The leaked renders show curved glass on the front and back with two horizontally placed cameras at the back. We’re also seeing what appears to be a hole-punch selfie camera on the screen, reminiscent of present-day Android phones. The iPhone is expected to see a radical shakeup this year, with Apple’s first-ever foldable likely to be revealed during the fall event next month. However, the company will reach a bigger milestone in 2027, marking 20 years since the first iPhone was revealed in 2007. A new leak is giving us our first potential look at the next-gen iPhone model Apple could introduce to celebrate. Leaker Yogesh Brar shares a couple of images on X that appear to show the 20th anniversary iPhone from multiple angles, including a clear view of its sides. It also appears to show a quad curved display on the front and a similarly curved glass on the rear panel. The images reveal dual rear cameras positioned horizontally, rather than vertically as on the iPhone 17. But for as interesting as all that is, it’s also hard to ignore some of the discrepancies in this particul…

title: ESPN’s streaming plans are getting more expensive: Here’s what you’ll pay
summary: Bundles including Disney Plus and Hulu are also affected.
body: TL;DR ESPN streaming plans and bundles are increasing in price. Plans are increasing by $1 to $3 per month. Adjustments also affect many streaming bundles that include ESPN. Last week, we learned that Verizon will soon increase the prices for its Disney Plus, ESPN, and Hulu perks , with plan add-ons increasing by a buck or two per month starting in September. Now, ESPN has announced that its streaming subscriptions and the bundles they’re included in will be going up in price for everyone, not just Verizon subscribers. As we’ve learned from 9to5Mac , ESPN has announced price hikes for its ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited streaming plans. Select is increasing from $13 to $14 per month (or $140 per year, up from $130), while Unlimited is jumping from $30 to $32 per month (or $320 per year, from $300). Bundles including ESPN along with Disney Plus and Hulu are going up, too.

title: Microsoft will pay you to get your friends using Edge
summary: Get 500 points for every successful referral.
body: TL;DR Microsoft is rolling out a referral program that gives Edge users 500 Microsoft Rewards points for every successful referral. You can earn up to 7,500 points per month, worth roughly $6.82 toward Microsoft or Xbox gift cards. Referrals only count when a new Edge Mobile user installs through your link and searches with Edge on two different days within 14 days. summary: The update adds a visual timeline indicator when double-tapping to skip.
body: TL;DR YouTube may be rolling out a new seek UI on Android that shows how much time you’ve skipped through a video. The change appears on the stable YouTube app, but it hasn’t reached every device. The new behavior could be part of a broader YouTube UI refresh. YouTube’s interface has become something of a moving target lately. The company was only recently testing a new button arrangement on Android that removed text labels from the controls under videos. And now, a small change to how YouTube shows skipped time appears to be rolling out to some Android users. The change involves YouTube’s familiar double-tap gesture for skipping. Currently, you can double-tap the right side of the screen to jump forward or the left side to rewind, while touching and holding the scrub bar lets you manually move through the video. In the current UI, double-tapping skips forward or backward without showing how much time you’ve moved. title: Chrome’s new rules ruined ad blockers. Here are 4 things that still work
summary: You can still block ads — just not how you used to.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority A few years ago, Chrome introduced Manifest V3 and began phasing out the older Manifest V2 technology used by some of the most advanced browser extensions. According to Google, the older version was harder to maintain and had its own real security risks, but we suspect it’s also because Google wanted to rein in extension capabilities. Unfortunately, this also made it harder to install extensions like the highly popular uBlock Origin. While workarounds still existed by using Chrome flags, that’s no longer the case . It is now virtually impossible to get MV2 extensions to work in Chrome.

title: 6 Android phones with microSD card slots you can still buy in 2026
summary: Say "no" to overpriced storage.
body: The smartphone industry is finally feeling the full effect of RAMageddon in 2026, as prices have shot up across the board due to rising memory costs. Brands are no longer able (or unwilling) to absorb the higher cost of components, so this is now passed on to us, the consumers. Smartphones with higher RAM and storage now command a steep premium, even more so than before. Thankfully, a small segment of smartphones still exists that has a solution for the storage crisis — the microSD card slot. It’s mostly entry-level and a few mid-range Android phones that still support the microSD card, but there are some good models to choose from. Flagship Android phones have largely done away with this feature, except for a few specialized models that aren’t widely available in the US.

title: I’m quitting Kindle, and Amazon’s new DRM update proves why you should too
summary: I’m finally ready to leave the Kindle world behind.
body: The Kindle Oasis was released in 2019, and it’s been a while since Amazon added a meaningful update to the system. So, when I learned that Amazon was rolling out a new system software update this past week, I was quite excited. That’s until I learned that the update closes a long-standing loophole for library books borrowed via Libby that lets you hold onto a book longer than you’d otherwise be allowed. Additionally, it further tightens DRM to ensure buyers can’t offload books from the Kindle. While the first feature doesn’t affect me much, the latter, as someone who likes preserving digital media, makes the update an instant no-go for me. On paper, these changes protect publishers’ rights and intellectual property. For the end user, though, they are just another reminder that you never truly own your digital library or even the hardware you technically bought.
